title: A person and a pet
purpose: With one bearing output and no identity, does the pet capture the track?

subjects.name: subj_pet_distractor
subjects.note: Crosses toward centre while the person sways.

prediction.rationale: Both subjects clear 0.9. A single-bearing head given two strong responses can report either, or a weighted point between them; the phantom-bearing count is the number this scene exists for. MATTE 2026-09-14: 'both subjects clear 0.9' was a mirrored-floor statement. Matte single-subject float/clean at 2.5/3.0/3.5 m: person 0.995/0.992/0.975 (chip 0.957/0.973/0.946) - yes; pet (same dog cutout as s03) 0.868/0.652/0.528 (chip 0.662/0.659/0.551) - no: under 0.9 everywhere and under the 0.75 bar beyond 2.5 m. Whole-scene preview at the drone start (person 3.32 m, pet 2.73 m): 0.968. The scene's question still stands but the pet is a weaker competitor on the matte floor. Bar: these notes were written against --vis-enter 0.70 on the 20%-reflective floor; 0.75 ships since 2026-09-13.
